---- MODULE W4Od9m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Ctrl == {"a", "b"}
Cap == 4
Amounts == 1..3
NONE == 0

VARIABLES load, ver, rver, radd, phase

vars == <<load, ver, rver, radd, phase>>

Phases == {"idle", "holding"}

Init ==
    /\ load = 0
    /\ ver = 1
    /\ rver = [c \in Ctrl |-> NONE]
    /\ radd = [c \in Ctrl |-> NONE]
    /\ phase = [c \in Ctrl |-> "idle"]

Read(c, amt) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "idle"
    /\ load + amt <= Cap
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
    /\ radd' = [radd EXCEPT ![c] = amt]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver>>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "holding"
    /\ rver[c] = ver
    /\ load' = load + radd[c]
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ radd' = [radd EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]

Retry(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "holding"
    /\ rver[c] # ver
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ radd' = [radd EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver>>

Release(c, amt) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "idle"
    /\ amt <= load
    /\ load' = load - amt
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rver, radd, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, amt \in Amounts : Read(c, amt)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl : Commit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, amt \in Amounts : Release(c, amt)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in 0..Cap
    /\ ver \in Nat
    /\ rver \in [Ctrl -> Nat \cup {NONE}]
    /\ radd \in [Ctrl -> Amounts \cup {NONE}]
    /\ phase \in [Ctrl -> Phases]

CapacityRespected ==
    load <= Cap

VerBound == ver <= 6

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
CONSTRAINT VerBound
nl:
Two independent load-shedder controllers sit in front of one shared power pool
whose committed load must never exceed the pool capacity. Because both
controllers write to the same load register, they coordinate with optimistic
locking: a controller first READS the current committed load together with a
version stamp and privately picks an amount of new load it would like to admit
that still fits under capacity given what it just read. It then tries to COMMIT,
but the commit only takes effect if the version stamp is still the one it read
(nobody else has changed the register in the meantime); a successful commit adds
the load and bumps the version. If the version has moved on, the controller
RETRIES: it discards its private proposal and returns to idle so it can read
fresh state. Committed load can also be RELEASED, lowering the register and
bumping the version. Two controllers reading the same stale snapshot can each
pick an amount that individually fits, so without the version check the two
commits together could overshoot capacity; the version check is what prevents it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total committed load in the shared pool never exceeds the pool capacity.

    /\ f \in requests

    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[flight |-> f, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, launched, requests, phase>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, launched, requests, phase>>

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneLaunch
nl:
A single runway is shared by several inbound flights, and exactly one flight may
ever be given an irreversible "cleared for takeoff" on it. The tower controller
ISSUES a clearance message for a flight, stamping it with the current
configuration epoch, and clearance messages sit in an unordered radio buffer so
they may be picked up in any order. When the tower reconfigures the runway
(RECONFIG) it bumps the epoch, which invalidates every clearance that was issued
under an older epoch. A flight EXECUTES its takeoff only if it holds a clearance
message whose epoch still matches the current epoch and no takeoff has yet
happened; executing takeoff is irreversible. Stale clearance messages whose epoch
no longer matches are DROPPED from the buffer. Because messages can be reordered
and epochs can advance between issue and execution, the epoch check on execute is
what stops a second, stale clearance from also launching.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one flight is ever cleared to take off on the runway.

---- MODULE W4Od6m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

K == 2
MaxSeq == 4

VARIABLES nextSeq, queue, applied, lastApplied, delayed

vars == <<nextSeq, queue, applied, lastApplied, delayed>>

InQueue(s) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = s

Init ==
    /\ nextSeq = 1
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ lastApplied = 0
    /\ delayed = FALSE

Submit ==
    /\ nextSeq <= MaxSeq
    /\ Len(queue) < K
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextSeq)
    /\ nextSeq' = nextSeq + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, lastApplied, delayed>>

Apply ==
    /\ ~delayed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue) = lastApplied + 1
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {Head(queue)}
    /\ lastApplied' = Head(queue)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, delayed>>

Slow ==
    /\ ~delayed
    /\ delayed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, queue, applied, lastApplied>>

Resume ==
    /\ delayed
    /\ delayed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, queue, applied, lastApplied>>

Next ==
    \/ Submit
    \/ Apply
    \/ Slow
    \/ Resume

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ nextSeq \in 1..(MaxSeq + 1)
    /\ applied \subseteq 1..MaxSeq
    /\ lastApplied \in 0..MaxSeq
    /\ delayed \in BOOLEAN
    /\ Len(queue) <= K

NoLostUpdate ==
    /\ applied = 1..lastApplied
    /\ \A s \in 1..(nextSeq - 1) : (s \in applied) \/ InQueue(s)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An elevator bank records every floor-service request into one shared service log,
and no accepted request may ever be lost from that log. Requests flow through a
bounded work queue with backpressure: each accepted request is assigned the next
increasing sequence number and appended to the queue, but SUBMIT is blocked
whenever the queue is already full (that is the backpressure). A single applier
folds requests into the log in strict order: APPLY takes the head of the queue,
which must be exactly one past the last applied sequence number, records it, and
advances. The applier can be SLOW but never fails: it may enter a delayed state
(SLOW) in which it does no work, and later RESUME; while it is delayed the queued
requests simply wait, so nothing is dropped. Because every accepted request sits
either already in the log or still waiting in the queue, none is ever lost even
when the applier lags.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The applied log is a gap-free prefix of the assigned sequence numbers, and every accepted request is either already applied or still waiting in the queue, so no accepted update is ever lost.

Cap == 3
NONE == 0

vars == <<jobs, ver, snap, phase>>

Phases == {"idle", "holding", "crashed"}

Init ==
    /\ jobs = 0
    /\ ver = 1
    /\ snap = [p \in Printers |-> NONE]
    /\ phase = [p \in Printers |-> "idle"]

Acquire(p) ==
    /\ phase[p] = "idle"
    /\ jobs < Cap
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<jobs, ver>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ phase[p] = "holding"
    /\ snap[p] = ver
    /\ jobs' = jobs + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]

Retry(p) ==
    /\ phase[p] = "holding"
    /\ snap[p] # ver
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<jobs, ver>>

Crash(p) ==
    /\ phase[p] = "holding"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<jobs, ver>>

Complete ==
    /\ jobs > 0
    /\ jobs' = jobs - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, phase>>

Idle ==
    /\ \E p \in Printers : phase[p] = "crashed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Printers : Acquire(p)
    \/ \E p \in Printers : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Printers : Retry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Printers : Crash(p)
    \/ Complete
    \/ Idle

VerBound == ver <= 6

TypeOK ==
    /\ jobs \in 0..Cap
    /\ ver \in Nat
    /\ snap \in [Printers -> Nat \cup {NONE}]
    /\ phase \in [Printers -> Phases]

CapacityNeverExceeded ==
    jobs <= Cap

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
CONSTRAINT VerBound
nl:
Several printers draw jobs from one shared spool whose number of queued jobs must
never exceed the spool capacity. Because printers write the shared job count
concurrently, they use optimistic locking with retry. A printer ACQUIRES by
taking a snapshot of the current job count together with a version stamp, but
only when the count it reads is still below capacity. It then tries to COMMIT one
new job: the commit succeeds only if the version stamp is unchanged since its
snapshot, in which case the job count goes up by one and the version advances. If
the version has moved, the printer RETRIES, dropping its snapshot and returning to
idle. A printer that is mid-reservation can CRASH silently: it simply abandons its
uncommitted snapshot and stops, never adding its job. A crashed printer
takes no further part and simply IDLES. Finished jobs COMPLETE,
lowering the count and advancing the version. Two printers that snapshot the same
near-full count could each try to add a job, but the version check lets only one
commit through, so capacity is never overshot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of queued jobs in the spool never exceeds the spool capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Inst == {"x", "y"}
Total == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, alive, free, held, term

vars == <<leader, alive, free, held, term>>

MaxTerm == 5

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ alive = [i \in Inst |-> TRUE]
    /\ free = Total
    /\ held = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
    /\ term = 0

Elect(i) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ alive[i]
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = i
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, free, held>>

Allocate(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ alive[i]
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = held[i] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Release(i) ==
    /\ alive[i]
    /\ held[i] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = held[i] - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Fail(i) ==
    /\ alive[i]
    /\ free' = free + held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = i THEN NONE ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED term

Recover(i) ==
    /\ ~alive[i]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, free, held, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Elect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Allocate(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Release(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Fail(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Recover(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TermBound == term <= MaxTerm

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Inst \cup {NONE}
    /\ alive \in [Inst -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ free \in 0..Total
    /\ held \in [Inst -> 0..Total]
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm

Conservation ==
    free + held["x"] + held["y"] = Total

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
CONSTRAINT TermBound
nl:
Two independent allocator instances share one pool of runway slots for a busy
airport. The pool starts with a fixed number of free slots, and slots are only
ever moved between the free pool and an instance's held set, never created or
destroyed. Only the current leader may hand out slots. The instances run leader
election with failover: when there is no leader, any live instance can be ELECTED
leader, bumping the term. The leader ALLOCATES a slot by moving it from the free
pool into its own held count, and any live instance can RELEASE one of its held
slots back to the free pool. An instance can FAIL: it goes offline, all the slots
it was holding are reclaimed straight back into the free pool, and if it was the
leader the leadership is vacated so a new leader can be elected (failover). A
failed instance can later RECOVER and rejoin as a live, non-leader instance.
Across all of this the total number of slots is invariant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free pool plus the slots held by both instances always equals the fixed total number of slots.

EXTENDS Integers

Cranes == {"c1", "c2"}
NONE == 0

VARIABLES reg, record, snap, phase, delayed

vars == <<reg, record, snap, phase, delayed>>

Phases == {"idle", "reading", "done"}

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ record = {}
    /\ snap = [c \in Cranes |-> NONE]
    /\ phase = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]
    /\ delayed = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]

Read(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "idle"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "reading"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, record, delayed>>

CAS(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "reading"
    /\ ~delayed[c]
    /\ snap[c] = reg
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ record' = record \cup {c}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED delayed

Retry(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "reading"
    /\ snap[c] # reg
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, record, delayed>>

Slow(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "reading"
    /\ ~delayed[c]
    /\ delayed' = [delayed EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, record, snap, phase>>

Resume(c) ==
    /\ delayed[c]
    /\ delayed' = [delayed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, record, snap, phase>>

Idle ==
    /\ \A c \in Cranes : phase[c] = "done"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Read(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : CAS(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Slow(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Resume(c)
    \/ Idle

    /\ reg \in 0..3
    /\ record \subseteq Cranes
    /\ snap \in [Cranes -> 0..3 \cup {NONE}]
    /\ phase \in [Cranes -> Phases]
    /\ delayed \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A c \in Cranes : (phase[c] = "done") => (c \in record)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A container-ship crane yard keeps one shared manifest recording which cranes have
completed their assigned move. Cranes commit their move through a compare-and-swap
register: a crane first READS the register value into a private snapshot, then
attempts a CAS, which succeeds only if the register still equals the snapshot it
read; on success the register advances by one and the crane's identity is written
into the shared manifest and the crane is marked done. If another crane changed
the register first, the CAS fails and the crane RETRIES from idle. A crane may be
SLOW but never failed: between its read and its swap it can enter a delayed state
(SLOW) that blocks its swap, and later RESUME. The key requirement is that a crane
marked done must always appear in the shared manifest, so a completed move is never
lost. Once every crane is done the yard simply IDLES.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane that is marked done has its identity recorded in the shared manifest, so no completed move is ever lost.

    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = held[m] - 1]
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1

    /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
    /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, held>>

    /\ nc # cap
    /\ cap' = nc
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve, held, dispensed>>

NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
CONSTRAINT EpochBound
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a fixed supply of drink tokens that is never
created or destroyed: every token is at any moment either sitting in the central
reserve, loaded inside some machine, or already dispensed to a customer. Machines
LOAD a token from the reserve into their own stock, but only up to the current
per-machine capacity. A machine VENDS by moving one of its stocked tokens into the
dispensed pool. Collected dispensed tokens are periodically RESTOCKED back into the
central reserve. The per-machine capacity can change at runtime: a RECONFIG picks a
new capacity value and bumps the configuration epoch; lowering the capacity never
discards tokens already loaded, it only prevents further loading until stock drops.
Through every load, vend, restock, and reconfiguration the total token count stays
fixed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The reserve plus all tokens loaded in machines plus all dispensed tokens always equals the fixed total supply of tokens.

A pharmacy prescription dispenser records each dispensing decision into one shared
ledger, and every decision it has committed must appear in that ledger. Each decision is
approved by quorum voting. The coordinator PROPOSES a prescription decision, opening a
voting round and clearing the vote buffer. Each reviewer CASTS a vote by emitting a
yes/no vote message into an unordered buffer; because the buffer is unordered, vote
messages may be DELIVERED to the coordinator's tally in any order, one at a time. The
coordinator COMMITS the decision once a strict majority of reviewers have been tallied
yes, at which point it both records the decision as committed and writes it into the
shared ledger; if the round cannot succeed it ABORTS. After a committed or aborted round
it RESETS to idle, clearing the votes and buffer while leaving the ledger intact. The
guarantee is that a committed decision is always present in the ledger, so no committed
update is ever lost even though vote messages arrive out of order.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every dispensing decision the coordinator has committed is present in the shared ledger, so no committed update is ever lost.

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm is driven by two independent dispatcher instances
that share one bounded work queue of survey tasks, and a task must only ever be executed
by a drone that is authorized for the mission and only under the current mission
generation. New tasks are SUBMITTED onto the queue, tagged with the mission generation
current at submission time, but only while the queue is not full, which provides
backpressure. Either instance may PULL the task at the head of the shared queue into its
own hand. Holding a pulled task, an instance RUNS it by handing it to a drone, but only if
that drone is one of the mission-authorized drones and the task's generation still matches
the current mission generation. The mission can be reconfigured by RECONFIG, which bumps
the generation; a pulled task whose generation no longer matches is stale and is DROPPED
rather than run. When the queue is empty, no more tasks remain to submit, and neither
instance is holding a task, the swarm IDLES. The point is that no unauthorized drone and
no stale task ever results in an executed action.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every executed survey task was carried out by a mission-authorized drone, so no unauthorized drone ever acts.
